comparison: Both address the puncta observation after cholesterol depletion (C53-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanism, while peer reviewers are SUPPORTED, accepting the observation and suggesting the puncta are likely D4 aggregates in cytosol after membrane cholesterol depletion.

Both evaluate protein interference claims (C41-C47). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with some uncertainty about in vitro to in vivo extrapolation. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, questioning why transiently expressed proteins would behave more correctly than microinjected ones and noting that exoplasmic leaflet binding may also suffer protein interference.

Both address mCherry-D4 binding and differential probe behavior (C49-C52). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with limited sample details noted. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, noting the finding has modest impact since fluorescent D4 fusions were previously reported, expressing concern about cell-to-cell variation, and requesting quantitative binding isotherms.

Both evaluate phospholipid composition effects on D4 binding (C21-C24, C31-C32). OpenEval finds claims well-SUPPORTED by Figure 1A data. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, requesting binding isotherms to clarify whether 'availability/accessibility' or Kd is changing, and cautioning against mischaracterization of Liu et al.'s work.

OpenEval R2 addresses acyl chain unsaturation effects (C29-C30, C63-C64) finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R1 encompasses these claims within broader phospholipid effects evaluation, expressing UNCERTAINTY and requesting binding isotherms to support quantitative conclusions about accessibility versus Kd changes.

Both address overall conclusions about D4 limitations (C33, C35-C36, C58, C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with some speculation noted about underestimation claims. Peer reviewers are SUPPORTED, agreeing the manuscript 'raises several valid concerns' and would provide 'a timely and clarifying contribution,' though requesting additional experiments for specific claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates the main conclusion (C9) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caution. Peer R5 addresses broader conclusions including C9, finding them SUPPORTED and noting the manuscript serves as a valid cautionary critique of Liu et al.'s methodology.

OpenEval R15 addresses hypotheses about protein interference (C41-C42) as SUPPORTED since they were subsequently tested. Peer R2 evaluates the experimental evidence for these claims as UNCERTAIN, questioning the interpretation and requesting quantitative comparisons.

Both reference cytoplasmic protein concentration (C43). OpenEval R3 finds this SUPPORTED as context for protein interference claims. Peer R6 is SUPPORTED, requesting additional citations to strengthen the reference base but not questioning the ~100 mg/ml estimate.

OpenEval finds characterization of Liu et al. methodology and conclusions (C3-C5, C12-C14, C38-C39) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these descriptive claims about prior work.
OpenEval finds background claims about cholesterol distribution consensus (C10-C11) SUPPORTED by established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these contextual claims.

OpenEval finds mechanistic context claims (C17-C18, C20, C26-C28) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims about prior D4 work (C40, C48) SUPPORTED by citations establishing context for Liu et al.'s negative results. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these contextual claims.

OpenEval finds claims about cholesterol flip-flop and probe-induced trapping (C56-C57, C69-C71) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these mechanistic context claims.

OpenEval finds biophysical principles about cholesterol-phospholipid interactions (C61-C62) SUPPORTED as established concepts. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these mechanistic background claims.

OpenEval finds hypotheses about differential DAN-D4 versus mCherry-D4 behavior (C65-C66) UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence testing relative protein-binding affinities. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval finds general framing claims (C1-C2, C25, C34, C59-C60, C67-C68, C72) SUPPORTED as established knowledge or appropriately cited contextual information. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims.
